title: Event broker shim and syntactic fidelity validator
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight broker shim and a fast syntactic fidelity validator for usage events entering the console analytics pipeline. Goal is to detect gross schema violations and apply best-effort enrichment/normalization at the edge to avoid noisy rejections, reduce downstream error troubleshooting, and enable partial-accept semantics for fields that can be deferred to a secondary validation pass.

Why: Production ingestion is seeing intermittent spikes of schema-variant payloads (new client SDK versions, truncation from proxies, and malformed tool-calls). Full semantic validation in the hot path increases latency and costs. We need a two-tier approach: (1) a sub-10ms syntactic validator + canonicalizer that rejects only obviously broken records and annotates soft-errors, and (2) a deferred semantic validator job that can accept/repair more complex cases asynchronously. The shim sits between the event broker (Kafka) and the existing consumer group to apply enrichment, backpressure signals, and consistent rejection semantics.

Scope: Implement broker shim (Scala/Kotlin service) with these features: lightweight field-level syntactic checks, canonical key mapping (known aliases -> canonical names), schema-version tagging, partial-accept headers, structured reject reasons, sticky sampling for deferred semantic validation, and backpressure propagation to producers via broker metrics and a simple rate-limit header. Add an opt-in feature flag under console config to route a percentage of traffic through the shim in staging and canary. Add observability and dashboards (ingest success/reject breakdown by reason, per-client schema drift trends, average repair rate by semantic job).

Non-goals: Full semantic validation inline, automated repair of arbitrary user payloads (beyond simple canonicalization/length truncation), or changing existing public telemetry contract without a deprecation window.

Architecture notes: Shim subscribes to source topic, runs syntactic checks, enriches events (client_id normalization, timestamp sanity correction), and writes to a downstream sanitized topic. The semantic validator job consumes sanitized topic and performs heavy checks and corrective transforms, emitting audit events for repaired records. Backpressure: shim monitors downstream consumer lag and starts emitting 'ingest-delay' metrics and a X-RateLimit-Suggested header when configured.

Security: shim will not store PII and will respect KMS encryption in transit. Feature is gated by release flag and audited.

Deliverables: code for shim service, canonicalization ruleset, staging canary config, dashboards, integration tests, rollout playbook and rollback criteria.
updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting. Attendees: Aisha (PM), Liam (ENG), Priya (Infra), Marco (Analytics). Agreed API shape for structured reject reasons. Action: Liam to prototype canonicalizer ruleset.

2026-02-25: Prototype complete. Syntactic validator implemented with JSON schema-lite checks (required fields, types, max-length). Benchmarked at 6-9ms median on staging messages. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/281

2026-03-02: Design decision logged: adopt partial-accept approach (accept record with annotated soft-errors) to keep user-visible failure rate low. Deferred semantic validation will flag and repair where possible.
2026-03-05: Metrics instrumentation agreed: reject_reason, repair_action, canonicalizations_applied, downstream_lag_ms. Dashboard proto created: /dashboards/usage-ingest-health

2026-03-09: Integration test harness updated to replay 7 days of sampled production traffic. Observed that canonicalizer fixes ~3.8% of records (mostly alias mapping), syntactic rejects ~0.4%. Added additional rule to correct mis-typed timestamps.
2026-03-12: Canaries planned for 2026-03-16: 5% of production traffic in us-west then 20% after 24h if error delta <= 0.2% and p95 latency delta <= 120ms.
acceptance_criteria: Syntactic validator rejects only when (a) required field missing, (b) gross type mismatch, or (c) payload parses as non-JSON. Rejects must include structured reason and error code.
Canonicalizer maps at least the current alias table (client_id, sdk_version, route) and preserves unknown keys without mutation.
End-to-end median added latency < 12ms for shim path in staging at 95th percentile of message sizes.
Dashboards show clear reject/repaired counts and per-client schema drift. Alerts fire when syntactic rejects rise > 0.5% over baseline.
Automated integration tests that replay sampled traffic pass in staging; semantic validator jobs mark repairs and emit audit events.
testing_plan: unit+integration tests for canonicalizer and shim
synthetic replay with production traffic profile (10% traffic) in staging
chaos test for schema drift and broker lag
notes: Decision: prefer partial-acceptance with structured reject reasons to reduce customer-visible failures.
Trade-off: richer validation vs. ingest latency — initial deployment uses fast syntactic checks and deferred semantic validation job.
Follow-up: schedule post-rollout review to consider moving some semantic checks inline if cost/latency acceptable.
